listed_sector_signals.signal: Steel, cement, and pulp & paper named as reference industries where energy-consumption-per-production indicators are used, offered as comparators for the mining sector (mentioned only, no application here)
listed_sector_signals.quote:
such as via the analysis of energy 
performance using specific consumption indicators that 
correlate energy consumption and production data, as seen 
in industries such as steel, cement, paper, and pulp [14].

other_continuous_flow_signals.signal: Iron ore pelletizing described as an energy-intensive thermal process (combustion-based pellet formation plus comminution, pumping, ventilation); the paper's data are aggregated with, but explicitly disaggregated from, this pelletizing sector
other_continuous_flow_signals.quote:
The pelletization process requires a significant 
amount of energy, both thermal—related to the combustion 
processes necessary for the physical–chemical formation of 
pellets—and electrical—used in comminution, pumping, 
and ventilation processes [39].

other_continuous_flow_signals.signal: Agglomeration processes (sintering and pelletization) referenced for iron ore fines destined for blast furnaces
other_continuous_flow_signals.quote:
The latter two products, when used in blast furnaces, 
require agglomeration processes known as sintering and pel-
letization [10].

one_line: The paper empirically analyzes energy consumption and energy-performance indicators of Brazil's iron ore mining and beneficiation sector (2011–2020), an extractive/open-pit mining context that is out of Corpus B scope, and only references steel/cement/pulp-paper and the pelletizing sector in passing.
